findings.summary: The real-network acceptance runs a command absent from the exact binary it tells the operator to install.
findings.evidence: The acceptance installs the existing tag with `go install github.com/mvelosop/vloop/cmd/vloop@v0.15.0-rc.4`, then requires `vloop self-update`. The brief is B44 and the command is new in its Shape; `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` is 0.15.0-rc.4 today, and `internal/cli/root.go` registers only the commands currently built. Reinstalling that immutable tag cannot contain B44's new command. A checkout build cannot replace that acceptance either: the command refuses a Build with no module version in S1 step 2.
findings.fix: Choose an executable acceptance path with the operator: either test only after a release containing B44 exists (name that post-release step and accept the released version), or provide a deliberate pre-release/tag containing B44 before close. Then rewrite the expected current/latest versions to match that executable.

findings.summary: An explicit older or pre-release binary target is followed by unversioned plugin updates, so the command can knowingly leave the binary and plugin at different versions.
findings.evidence: The brief permits `--version <v>` to install an older version. S2 then runs `claude plugin update vloop@vloop --scope <scope>` and `copilot plugin update vloop@vloop` without a version. Doctor's S3 warning is still framed around a binary/plugin mismatch. For example, `--version v0.14.0` from v0.15.0-rc.4 downgrades the binary while S2 advances or retains plugins at the marketplace's current version.
findings.fix: Decide and pin what `--version` means for plugins. Either skip plugin updates and say so in human/JSON output, attempt to pin both agents to the same release (if their CLIs support it), or explicitly permit the mismatch and define the next-line and doctor behaviour. Add a literal worked example for the chosen case.

findings.summary: The B44 roadmap handover row is absent, and the brief falsely says B40-B43 rows already exist.
findings.evidence: The brief says its B44 row will be added only in a ready commit and compares this with B40-B43. `.claude/skills/vloop-architect/SKILL.md` says the active roadmap owns scope and the row points at the brief at handover. `docs/design-notes/vloop-roadmap-b18-b21.md` currently ends at B41; searches in `docs/design-notes/` find no B42 or B43 row.
findings.fix: Before marking the brief ready, add the B44 row to the active roadmap with its brief path, owned slice and dependency (and add B42/B43 rows if their queue order requires them), or remove the inaccurate B40-B43 comparison and name the actual predecessor rows.

decisions: Keep `vloop self-update` for machine-wide binary/plugin work and `vloop upgrade` for repository work; I agree with the separation.
Use the Go module channel (`go list -m -json ...@latest` and `go install ...@<version>`), not GitHub release assets; I agree.
Default updates are strictly forward, while explicit `--version` may select an older or pre-release version; the plugin consequence needs the operator decision above.
Refuse on missing Go, a devel/checkout build, or a binary outside Go's install destination; I agree.
Keep doctor and `vloop upgrade` offline; only `self-update` performs network-capable work; I agree.
Plugin failures are reported but non-fatal after the binary step; I agree.
Amend C-2 so paths outside a repository use slash-separated absolute/home-relative display; reasonable, and already carried into the brief.
Fake `go`, `claude` and `copilot`, use existing x/mod/semver, and define `--check --version`; these implementation choices are sound.
checked: facts: Build.Version versus Build.Module and devel detection in internal/cli/buildinfo.go, plugin version storage, doctor plugin discovery/warnings, release go list/go install usage, module dependency, schema embedding and path conventions; consistency: S1-S3, explicit version, human/JSON output and worked example; rules: C-1/C-2/C-3, B36, P-7/P-8 and architect roadmap handover; runnability: .vloop/config.toml's Go check, Windows fakes, command-doc regeneration in task 1, and acceptance reachability. `vloop brief check` on a ready copy passed structure with one expected warning for the new schemas/self-update.v1.json.
